correctness.rationale: The radius of curvature is exactly R-3a cos(2t)-24b sin(5t). Positivity at t and t+pi implies R>3|a|, hence lambda=-3a/R lies in (-1,1). The Wigner branch has signed support b sin(5t), giving five simple cusps modulo pi. The centre-symmetry-set cusp criterion reduces to 2x Q_lambda(x^2)=0. The exact discriminant of Q_lambda is positive throughout the relevant lambda interval away from the harmless degree drop at zero, the endpoint values never vanish, and exact sign witnesses plus the lambda=0 roots force exactly two simple Q-roots in (0,1). Thus there are exactly five ordinary CSS cusps. The packaged symbolic checker verifies every critical identity.

value.rationale: The general literature gives only an inequality between two cusp counts and isolated examples. The family studied here is not artificial: a concrete member is already used as a canonical illustration in the literature. Proving that every strictly convex member has exactly five cusps on both singular curves, and explaining this by an explicit cubic whose discriminant protects the count across the whole parameter chamber, gives a reusable structural model for the equality case rather than a routine recount of one diagram.
